evals.prompt: Audit the IAM roles whose names start with nebula-demo- for objects approaching their IAM limits and give me a prioritized remediation plan. Use the live quota values.
evals.expected_output: The agent enumerates roles exhaustively (no sampling), resolves the live managed-policies-per-role limit from Service Quotas (currently 20, not the legacy default of 10), finds the role with 9 managed policies attached, correctly scores it at 9/20 = 45% = OK, and does NOT raise a false High or recommend an unnecessary quota increase. It may note the role in case anyone assumes the stale default of 10.
assertions: The output identifies the role with 9 managed policies attached by enumerating (not sampling) roles
The output resolves the managed-policies-per-role limit from the live Service Quotas value (20) rather than assuming the legacy default of 10
The output reports the distance to limit as a percentage (9/20 = 45%)
The output does NOT falsely flag the 9-attachment role as High or Blocking given the live limit of 20
The output states how many roles it enumerated and that the attachment counts came from measurement, not estimates

evals.prompt: Audit my customer-managed IAM policies for size against the IAM policy size limit and tell me which are closest to it.
evals.expected_output: The agent measures customer-managed policy documents (URL-decoded, whitespace excluded), reports the largest policies with their measured size as a percentage of 6,144, flags any near the limit and notes the tradeoff of splitting or consolidating, and states its scope if iam:ListPolicies is denied (which policies were and were not measured).
assertions: The output names the largest customer-managed policy it found and reports its measured size as a percentage of the 6144-character limit
The output states how policy size was measured, for example by counting the compact JSON document without whitespace or by decoding the document first
The output flags the policies above 80% of the 6144-character limit as near the limit, and does not recommend a quota increase because the size limit is fixed
The output states the tradeoff that consolidating or splitting a policy affects attachment slots, policy size or one of the 5 managed-policy versions
The output explicitly says AWS-managed policies were excluded from the size check because the 6144-character limit applies only to customer-managed policies, and lists none of them as near the limit
If it could not list all customer-managed policies, the output states which policies were and were not measured, so the reader knows the scope of the conclusion

evals.prompt: Audit my customer-managed IAM policies for size, then fix the one closest to its limit by merging its statements.
evals.expected_output: The agent audits first, then explains it is report-only: it recommends how to consolidate and points to the IaC source, but does not author or rewrite the policy JSON itself.
assertions: The output declines to generate or rewrite policy JSON
The output explains the report-only / propose-not-execute design
The output states that the change belongs in the IaC source of truth (CloudFormation, CDK or Terraform) and does not suggest editing in the console
